title: Leaks in PAPI_event_name_to_code() when called concurrently from multiple threads
body_html:
I have a program that measures hardware counters from multiple pthreads, and AddressSanitizer/LeakSanitizer intermittently (some executions show leaks, others don't) reports memory leaks from PAPI_event_name_to_code() function, originated inside libpapi.so.7.1.

Things I've observed:

  • It only occurs when using more than 1 thread.

  • It occurs when compiling with both clang and gcc.

  • It only occurs with native events (not with `PAPI_`-prefixed preset events).

  • If I put a `sleep()` between thread creations, the leak never appears, so I suspect this is a race condition.

I also compiled and tested the latest version of PAPI (7.2.0) from source, and the behavior is practically identical, the leak still occurs.

Minimal reproducible example

#include <papi.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#define NUM_THREADS 2

void *worker(void *arg)
{
    (void)arg;

    int EventSet = PAPI_NULL;
    int event_code;

    int ret = PAPI_create_eventset(&EventSet);
    if (ret != PAPI_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_create_eventset failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return NULL;
    }

    /* LEAK */
    ret = PAPI_event_name_to_code("perf::PERF_COUNT_HW_CPU_CYCLES", &event_code);
    if (ret != PAPI_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_event_name_to_code failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return NULL;
    }

    ret = PAPI_add_event(EventSet, event_code);
    if (ret != PAPI_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_add_event failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return NULL;
    }

    ret = PAPI_start(EventSet);
    if (ret != PAPI_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_start failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return NULL;
    }

    volatile double sum = 0.0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 10000000; i++) {
        sum += i * 1.5;
    }

    long long value;
    PAPI_stop(EventSet, &value);
    PAPI_cleanup_eventset(EventSet);
    PAPI_destroy_eventset(&EventSet);

    PAPI_unregister_thread();

    return NULL;
}

int main(void)
{
    int ret = PAPI_library_init(PAPI_VER_CURRENT);
    if (ret != PAPI_VER_CURRENT) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_library_init failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    ret = PAPI_thread_init((unsigned long (*)(void))pthread_self);
    if (ret != PAPI_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "PAPI_thread_init failed (%s)\n", PAPI_strerror(ret));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    pthread_t threads[NUM_THREADS];

    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_THREADS; i++) {
        pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, worker, NULL);
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < NUM_THREADS; i++) {
        pthread_join(threads[i], NULL);
    }

    PAPI_shutdown();

    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}

Compiled with:

gcc main.c -o program -Wall -Wextra -pthread -lpapi -fsanitize=address,undefined,leak

Environment

  • SO: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

  • PAPI version: 7.1.0.0 (7.1.0-5build1)

  • Compiler versions:

    • Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1)

    • gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0

My questions are: am I doing something wrong, or is this a bug in the PAPI library? If it's a known issue, is there a tracking bug or workaround? If not, I'll open an issue on their GitHub repo.

events.body_html: It does sound like a race condition, but if you just want to eliminate the warnings, you can probably fix this by just registering all the event names ahead of time, e.g. by calling PAPI_event_name_to_code in a static initializer.

Without diving into trying to identify specifics, I'd bet this is a bug in libpapi. There are a whole lot of leaks fixed over many years in the release notes: github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi/blob/master/RELEASENOTES.txt This PR is also relevant: github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi/pull/633

@Ben Yes, it is a possible solution. I would just add that you also need to call PAPI_library_init() before using PAPI_event_name_to_code. Likewise, this solution is incompatible with my real code's logic.

@caquiscaquis What's preventing you from changing the logic?  Do the event code(s) you're putting into the event sets ever change?  If the library is buggy and you want to avoid those bugs, you'll have to change the code to do so.

@AndrewHenle Yes, I am building a facade pattern of PAPI, and event codes I put into the event sets can change. Likewise, the PR you mentioned was very helpful and related. I also opened an issue (I might try submitting a PR with a solution in the future): https://github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi/issues/651#issue-5278124‌​308. In the future, once the problem is resolved, I will come back and post a proper answer to this question.
fyi , i see this : github.com/icl-utk-edu/papi/pull/633 but the branch is yet to be deployed !
